$comment: Lint rules for intel-vt. Extracted verbatim from tools/lint.mjs when the linter became config-driven; behaviour is unchanged. Every regex is {re, flags} because an implicit flag set is how a rule silently stops matching.
$comment_claimFreeFiles: Empty on purpose. This skill's core-facts.md carries claim lines and is a sourced fact layer, not a pure index. The sibling amd-virtualization made the opposite choice; the rule is per-skill for exactly that reason.
$comment_unscopedNegative: Three fabricated negatives have reached this repository's corpora. README records the first two; amd-virtualization/references/errata.md E27 records the third, which stood in eight places and was refuted by that skill's own bibliography three lines below the assertion. The work contract already said a negative claim needs the same evidence as a positive one, and it did not prevent a third - so the rule is mechanical rather than advisory. A blanket 'no such document exists' must name a publication number, carry an as-of date, or live in 90-dated-landscape.md where it is re-checked. Applied to both skills because the defect class is not vendor-specific. Proved non-vacuous by injection before being committed.

patterns.re: (there (?:is|are) no public |\b(?:AMD|Intel|Microsoft|the vendor) publishes no \b|\b(?:AMD|Intel|Microsoft) has no public \b|\bno public [a-z\- ]{0,40}(?:guide|reference|PPR|document|documentation|specification|erratum|errata|copy|source) )

unscopedNegative.message: a negative claim needs the same evidence as a positive one, scoped to a document and a date (see amd-virtualization errata.md E27)

$comment_offSpec: Subjects that appear nowhere in the Intel SDM. A claim about one of these whose ONLY anchor is an SDM section is citation filler: the section number resolves, but to an unrelated subject. This defect reached 44 claims in chapter 15 before a PDF check caught it.

offSpec.message: the SDM does not document it
